title: Module Imports with Side-Effects
pattern: A module file contains global initialization blocks (e.g., `lazy_static!`, `ctor`, or static initializers) that perform network, file I/O, or thread-spawning side effects simply by being imported.
why_bad: It causes implicit side-effect coupling. Merely importing a library or compiling a file triggers active execution that can fail or hang, creating unpredictable build environments and test execution failures.
detection: Lazy or static initialization blocks that perform blocking system calls, read files, or establish network connections.
counterexample: Static compile-time constant arithmetic or pure local memory structures configured statically.
source: Eric Elliott, *Composing Software* (2019) ("Module imports with side-effects"); Michael Feathers, *Working Effectively with Legacy Code* (2004), Chapter 12 ("The Case of the Horrible Include Dependencies").
